decisions.reason: Requiring both stations to run simultaneously does not change the established matcha-mixing quality, foam, whisk, or positioning requirements.
The source requires simultaneous station operation but does not require simultaneous dispensing or change the existing per-station dispensing behavior.

Simultaneous operation of the two stations does not alter the existing motor durability or maximum-speed duty constraints; the several-minute demonstration condition belongs to the operational demonstration requirement.
A complete same-message MODIFY already records both stations running simultaneously and the other required demonstration elements.
The source asks that speed adjustment be demonstrated but does not change the existing speed range, maximum speed, or intended speed modes.
Simultaneous station operation has no necessary effect on whisk removal, clearance, or tool-free detachment behavior.
The source does not change bowl capacity, depth, geometry, refilling policy, or enclosure-size constraints.
Running both stations simultaneously does not alter the bowl removal, swapping, or clearance requirements.
The source does not add or change a splash-control condition for simultaneous operation.
The candidate already requires capacity for both motors, solenoids, and cooling fans to operate simultaneously, so the source introduces no new electrical-load state.
A complete same-message MODIFY already records the leak-free acceptance condition for both plumbing paths during continuous operation; simultaneous mixing adds no further plumbing change.
The simultaneous-operation decision does not affect the deferred accent-lighting requirement or any of its design attributes.
